explanation: The Laws set it at 11 m (12 yards). The penalty area reaches 16.5 m out, and the arc on its edge keeps other players 9.15 m (10 yards) from the penalty mark.

claims.text: Under the Laws of the Game, the penalty mark is 11 metres (12 yards) from the goal line, measured from the midpoint between the goalposts.
5.5 metres is the depth of the goal area, 9.15 metres is the radius of the penalty arc, and 16.5 metres is the depth of the penalty area; none is the distance to the penalty mark.
The penalty area extends 16.5 metres (18 yards) into the field from the goal line.
The penalty arc is drawn 9.15 metres (10 yards) from the penalty mark, so that other players stay at least that distance away during a penalty kick.
12 yards is about 11 metres and 10 yards is about 9.15 metres.

evidence.restatement: Law 1 of IFAB's Laws of the Game puts the penalty spot 11 m (12 yd) out from the goal line, on the line through the centre of the goal.

claimResults.note: Answered 11 metres cold. The pitch markings in Law 1 are long fixed; the penalty mark is 11 m from the midpoint between the posts. Certain knowledge, both-pass rule of memo 18.

evidence.restatement: The other three figures belong to other markings: the six-yard box is 5.5 m deep, the arc and the free-kick distance are 9.15 m, and the eighteen-yard box is 16.5 m deep.

claimResults.note: Each distractor is a real pitch measurement, so it tempts, but none is the spot's distance. All three definitely wrong.

evidence.restatement: The big box reaches 16.5 m (18 yd) from the goal line into the pitch.

claimResults.note: Law 1 marking; matches the 18-yard box name.

evidence.restatement: The penalty arc has a 9.15 m (10 yd) radius centred on the spot, because Law 14 keeps all other players at least that far from the mark while the kick is taken.

claimResults.note: Law 1 arc plus Law 14 positioning rule; the stated purpose is correct.
Pure conversions: 12 yd = 10.97 m (about 11 m) and 10 yd = 9.144 m (about 9.15 m, the rounded Laws figure).

evidence.restatement: The Laws of the Game put the penalty spot 11 m (12 yards) out from the goal line, centred between the posts.

claimResults.note: Rival test: 9.15 m is the arc and the wall distance, 16.5 m is the penalty area depth, 5.5 m the goal area; each belongs to a different line, none to the mark. High-risk numbers confirmed directly (memo 18).

evidence.restatement: The goal area reaches 5.5 m, the arc sits 9.15 m from the spot, and the penalty area reaches 16.5 m; none of these is the spot's distance.

claimResults.note: Each distractor is a real pitch measurement, so it tempts, yet is not the spot distance.

evidence.restatement: The big box extends 18 yards, or 16.5 m, from the goal line into the pitch.
The D-shaped arc outside the box is drawn 10 yards (9.15 m) from the spot so players keep that far back during a kick.

claimResults.note: 10.97 rounds to about 11 and 9.144 to about 9.15 (the Laws round it so); 'about' hedges it.

issues.note: The Laws say 11 m (12 yards) from the midpoint between the posts to the mark; 12 yards is actually 10.97 m, but 11 m is the Laws' own figure, so no one can defend another option.
